When each row already describes a point, pass the table straight to `hchart()`.
Use a `data_to_*` helper when you need to calculate boxplot statistics, count
transitions or reorganize rows into the structure a chart expects.

| What you have | Helper | What to do with the result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Several measurements per observation | `data_to_parallel_coordinates()` | Add one line per row with `hc_add_series_list()`. |
| A numeric measurement and optional groups | `data_to_boxplot()` | Add the boxes and optional outlier series with `hc_add_series_list()`. |
| One column per stage in a journey | `data_to_sankey()` | Pass the weighted links to `hchart(links, type = "sankey")`. |
| Nested groups and a numeric size | `data_to_hierarchical()` | Pass the nodes to `hchart(nodes, type = "treemap")` or `hchart(nodes, type = "sunburst")`. |
| Coordinates and text for labels | `data_to_annotation_labels()` | Pass the labels to `hc_add_annotation()` on an existing chart. |

```{r setup, message=FALSE}
library(highcharter)
hc_set_theme("hcrt", colors = hc_theme("smpl")$colors)
```

## Parallel coordinates

Each line represents one diamond in a reproducible sample of 1,200 from
`ggplot2::diamonds`. Read across the axes to compare weight, depth, table width
and price. Color follows the five ordered cut grades from Fair (purple) to
Ideal (yellow). Depth and table width are percentages.

```{r parallel-coordinates, eval=requireNamespace("ggplot2", quietly = TRUE)}
set.seed(42)
ids <- sample.int(nrow(ggplot2::diamonds), 1200)
diamonds <- ggplot2::diamonds[ids, ]
series <- data_to_parallel_coordinates(
  diamonds[c("carat", "depth", "table", "price")],
  name = paste0("Diamond #", ids, " · ", diamonds$cut),
  color = hex_to_rgba(colorize(diamonds$cut), alpha = 0.18)
)

highchart() |>
  hc_chart(type = "line", parallelCoordinates = TRUE) |>
  hc_xAxis(
    categories = c("Weight (ct)", "Depth (%)", "Table (%)", "Price (USD)")
  ) |>
  hc_add_series_list(series) |>
  hc_plotOptions(
    series = list(
      animation = FALSE,
      marker = list(enabled = FALSE),
      states = list(inactive = list(enabled = FALSE))
    )
  ) |>
  hc_tooltip(
    formatter = JS(
      "function () {
    const axes = this.series.xAxis.categories;
    const rows = this.series.points.map(p => {
      const row = axes[p.x] + ': ' + Highcharts.numberFormat(p.y, -1);
      return p.x === this.x ? '<b>' + row + '</b>' : row;
    });
    return ['<b>' + this.series.name + '</b>', ...rows].join('<br>');
  }"
    )
  )
```

Hover over a line to see its cut grade and all four measurements. Each axis
uses its own scale. Disabling the inactive state keeps the other diamonds at
their original opacity as you move the pointer.

## Boxplots

To compare petal lengths across species, let the helper calculate one box
per group. With `add_outliers = TRUE`, it also returns a scatter series for
the observations beyond the whiskers. Click the legend to hide or show the
boxes and their outliers together.

```{r boxplots}
boxes <- data_to_boxplot(
  iris,
  Petal.Length,
  Species,
  add_outliers = TRUE,
  name = "Petal length",
  color = hc_theme("smpl")$colors[[1]]
)

highchart() |>
  hc_chart(style = list(fontFamily = "IBM Plex Sans", fontWeight = "300")) |>
  hc_xAxis(categories = levels(iris$Species)) |>
  hc_yAxis(title = list(text = "Petal length (cm)")) |>
  hc_legend(itemStyle = list(fontWeight = "300")) |>
  hc_add_series_list(boxes)
```

## Sankey links

Which airlines connected New York's three airports to the Midwest? Each row
is one flight with a recorded arrival in January 2013 at one of six selected
destinations. Order the columns as origin → airline → destination.
`data_to_sankey()` counts the flights between each pair of adjacent stages.
For example, the links into Chicago O’Hare (ORD) sum to 1,230 arrivals.

```{r sankey-links}
flights <- read.csv("data/nyc-midwest-flights.csv.gz")
links <- data_to_sankey(flights[c("origin", "carrier", "dest")])

hchart(links, "sankey", name = "Flights", nodeWidth = 14, nodePadding = 12) |>
  hc_title(text = "From New York to the Midwest") |>
  hc_subtitle(text = "3,445 flights · January 2013") |>
  hc_tooltip(valueDecimals = 0)
```

[Flight data from nycflights13](https://nycflights13.tidyverse.org/) ·
[Download the three flight columns](data/nyc-midwest-flights.csv.gz).
The same layout can display [parallel sets in D3](https://observablehq.com/@d3/parallel-sets).

## Hierarchy nodes

Count Pokémon by primary and secondary type. `data_to_hierarchical()` turns
each primary type into a parent node and each observed combination into a
leaf. Pokémon with a single type get their own leaf, such as “Only Electric”.

In this [treemap from Showcase](showcase.html#pokemon), the area of each
rectangle shows the number of Pokémon. Click a primary type to explore its
secondary types.

```{r hierarchy-nodes, code=readLines(system.file("examples", "pokemon.R", package="highcharter"), encoding="UTF-8")}
```

## Annotation labels

Stage 8 of the 2017 Tour de France has three kinds of landmarks: towns,
summits and climbs. Each row supplies its distance (`x`), elevation (`y`) and
label (`text`). Convert each table with the same helper, then give its labels
a placement suited to the terrain. Here 12 labels share a single elevation series.

[Original annotated stage profile](https://jkunst.com/blog/posts/2020-06-02-30diasdegraficos-parte-3/) ·
[Download the elevation profile (CSV)](data/tour-2017-stage-8.csv).

```{r tour-elevation}
stage <- read.csv("data/tour-2017-stage-8.csv")
towns <- data.frame(
  x = c(27.98, 45.5, 63, 84, 129.5, 159),
  y = c(255, 611, 651, 789, 382, 443),
  text = c(
    "Arbois",
    "Montrond",
    "Mont-sur-Monnet",
    "Bonlieu",
    "Chassal",
    "Saint-Claude"
  )
)
climbs <- data.frame(
  x = c(96.2, 134.5, 172.2),
  y = c(783, 540, 925),
  text = c("6.1 km · 4.6%", "7.6 km · 5.2%", "11.7 km · 6.4%")
)
summits <- data.frame(
  x = c(101.44, 138.5, 176.4),
  y = c(1026, 748, 1202),
  text = c(
    "Col de la Joux",
    "Côte de Viry",
    "Montée de la Combe<br>de Laisia Les Molunes"
  )
)

hchart(
  stage,
  "area",
  hcaes(distance, elevation),
  name = "Elevation",
  fillOpacity = 0.25
) |>
  hc_title(text = "Tour de France 2017 · Stage 8") |>
  hc_xAxis(title = list(text = "Distance (km)")) |>
  hc_yAxis(title = list(text = "Elevation (m)")) |>
  hc_tooltip(valueSuffix = " m") |>
  hc_add_annotation(
    labels = data_to_annotation_labels(towns),
    labelOptions = list(
      verticalAlign = "top",
      y = 10,
      backgroundColor = "rgba(255,255,255,0.85)"
    )
  ) |>
  hc_add_annotation(labels = data_to_annotation_labels(summits)) |>
  hc_add_annotation(
    labels = data_to_annotation_labels(climbs),
    labelOptions = list(shape = "connector", align = "right", x = -8, y = -32)
  )
```
